claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance and oxidizes rapidly at high temperature.
The proposed intervention is pack aluminizing in an Al-rich powder mixture at approximately 1000 °C for approximately 4 hours.
Controlled cooling and the selected thermal cycle will limit deep Al diffusion and preserve the substrate composition.
Pack aluminizing will produce a continuous external alumina scale on HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina scale produced by pack aluminizing will be well-adherent.
The alumina scale produced by pack aluminizing will be nanostructured.
Al from the pack will diffuse into the superficial layer of HfNbTaTiZr.
Al in the superficial layer will react with oxygen to form a slow-growing Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier that minimizes oxygen ingress into the bulk alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress will prevent oxidation-induced deterioration of the alloy.
Pack aluminizing will leave the underlying BCC microstructure unaltered.
Pack-aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will have substantially improved oxidation resistance during exposure to air at 1000 °C.
After treatment and high-temperature air exposure, the alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After treatment and high-temperature air exposure, the alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Extensive Al diffusion or alumina-scale spallation could compromise the intended surface-confined treatment and mechanical-property retention.
